title: A receipt printer
description:
Write `formatReceipt(items, tipPercent)`, which turns a list of items into the text of a receipt:

```javascript
formatReceipt([
  { name: "Green tea", price: 2.5, qty: 2 },
  { name: "Chocolate cake", price: 4.25, qty: 1 },
], 10)
```

```
Green tea x2           5.00
Chocolate cake         4.25
---------------------------
Subtotal               9.25
Tip 10%                0.93
Total                 10.18
```

Rules:
- Each item line is the name, followed by ` x<qty>` when the quantity is more than 1, padded on the right to 19 characters, then the line total (price × qty) with 2 decimals right-aligned in 8 characters. Names longer than 19 characters (with the quantity) are cut to 18 characters plus `…`.
- Then a line of 27 dashes, then `Subtotal`, `Tip <percent>%` and `Total` lines in the same layout. The tip is the subtotal × percent / 100, **rounded to cents**; the total is subtotal + tip.
- With a tip of 0, the tip line is left out.
- To avoid floating-point errors, work in whole cents: `Math.round(price * 100)`.
- Items with a quantity of 0 or less are skipped. If no items are left, the receipt is just `No items`.
- Lines are joined with `\n` (no newline at the end).
hints: Write one small helper that formats a label and an amount in cents into a line; every line of the receipt then uses it.
`Math.round(price * 100)` turns a price into whole cents once; after that, all sums are exact integers.
requirements: Item lines, quantities, cutting long names and alignment follow the rules.
Totals are exact to the cent, with the tip rounded.
Zero tips and empty receipts are handled.
stretch: Add tax by category (food 10%, other 20%) with a line per rate, and a `currency` option using `Intl.NumberFormat`.
